reasoning: Recent Georgia polling in the last 45 days consistently shows **Jon Ossoff (D)** leading **Mike Collins (R)** in the 2026 Senate race by mid‑single to low‑double digits, with the most recent poll putting Ossoff at about **D+7**. Taken together, these polls and forecaster write‑ups indicate the **current Senate race environment is D+7–9 and rated Lean/Likely Democratic**, while Georgia’s structural Cook PVI remains slightly Republican at R+1, underscoring that Democrats are favored in 2026 despite a narrow GOP-leaning baseline. I did not find fresh, state-specific general-election presidential polling for Georgia within the last 45 days, so the current measurable margin applies to the Senate race only, not the presidential race.

sources.name: AARP / Fabrizio Ward & Impact Research
sources.details: AARP/Fabrizio Ward & Impact Research poll of 1,060 likely Georgia voters found Jon Ossoff 52% to Mike Collins 43%, a D+9 margin in the 2026 U.S. Senate race.

sources.name: Atlanta Journal-Constitution
sources.details: Atlanta Journal-Constitution coverage of the AARP poll reports Ossoff leading Collins 52% to 43% in the Georgia Senate race, describing him as leading in one of the state’s top contests.

sources.details: Roll Call’s "At the Races" column summarizes the AARP poll showing Ossoff with a 9-point lead over Collins and characterizes Georgia as one of the most consequential Senate races where Democrats are currently ahead.

sources.details: The Hill reports on the AARP survey, stating that Ossoff leads Collins by 9 points, 52% to 43%, with the lead outside the poll’s 3-point margin of error.

sources.details: Newsweek cites a Wick poll showing Ossoff up 4 points over Collins, 46.7% to 42.9%, indicating a narrower but still positive margin for Democrats in the Georgia Senate race.

sources.details: InsiderAdvantage poll, as reported by WRDW, finds Ossoff at 50% and Collins at 43% among likely voters, a D+7 margin in the Georgia Senate race.
